races.name: Iglu Apprentice Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Ambishio
runners_data.note: Hold-up specialist who has run all five recent starts over this exact 5f trip on good ground, recording a placed effort last time out 11 days ago; headgear (hp) flags a horse that needs to be switched on, and Michael Appleby's yard is in modest form (4/35 over 14 days), but the consistent course-and-distance profile makes this the horse best equipped to handle a sprint finish.
runners_data.comment: Won earlier in this six-start sequence and rated 83 by us, clear of this field, Ambishio already has today's distance covered and returns after just 11 days under 140 lb. His finishes since, including a fifth last time out, have been more mixed.

runners_data.name: London Is Blue
runners_data.note: Returned two wins from three runs on good ground in summer 2024 and has strong form over 5-6f, making it well-suited in terms of conditions; 79 days off is a notable concern on fitness grounds, but Robert Cowell's light yard strike rate (1/8 over 14 days) and Jack Callan's ability to adapt tactics in a pace-less race could see this horse edge into a forward pitch that its natural closing style wouldn't normally warrant.
runners_data.comment: Two wins earlier in this sequence of five starts show real ability and he already has today's distance covered, but a below-par fourth last time out, a lengthy 79-day absence since, and the lowest of our four ratings here are the concerns.

runners_data.name: Adalida
runners_data.note: Recorded a win over this exact trip on good going two runs ago and holds genuine ability at the level, but the horse's true running style is deeper than midfield — placed there on the pace map only because the field carries a surplus of hold-up types; Ethan Tindall's 3lb claim helps on weight, though the style-fit score of 0.92 reflects the risk of being shuffled wide or late in a compressed 5f sprint.
runners_data.comment: Runner-up last time out and with a win among her last six starts, she already has today's distance covered and returns after a moderate 18-day break. Our rating of 73 leaves her third of this quartet, with a couple of rivals fancied ahead of her.

runners_data.name: Victor Cee
runners_data.note: Lowest-rated runner in the field (OR 64) with a headgear flag (v) suggesting concentration issues, and only one win and two places from twelve starts on similar going; like Adalida, this is a true closer placed into midfield on the map due to the field's pace surplus — the style-fit discount of 0.90 is meaningful, and 29 days since last run adds a further layer of uncertainty over a sharp 5f trip.
runners_data.comment: Yet to win in five starts, though a third was his best effort, and our rating of 76 - well clear of his 64 official mark - makes him second in this field with today's trip already covered. He returns after a 29-day break, the one query.

races.paceDynamic: With all four runners carrying a hold-up profile, this 5f sprint at Yarmouth has no natural front-runner to set the tempo, meaning the field will almost certainly drift into an uncontrolled, dawdling early gallop before erupting into a furious sprint finish in the final two furlongs. Ambishio and London Is Blue are the most experienced closers here, both with proven form at this trip on good ground, and their ability to quicken from a slow pace will be tested equally. The field holds more genuine hold-up types than the pace map can place at the rear — Adalida and Victor Cee are true deep closers redistributed into midfield, meaning they are unlikely to get a clean, unimpeded late run if the sprint bunches. This shape heavily favours the horse who can travel closest to the pace without losing their position, then produce the sharpest acceleration over the final furlong — a prominent-to-mid-division profile with tactical speed is the clear beneficiary.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Sprint Bunches, Quickest Wins
scenarios.trigger: If the field crawls early and erupts into a wall-to-wall dash over the final 2f with no runner getting a clear advantage.
scenarios.body: Ambishio and London Is Blue, both proven over 5f on good ground, are best equipped to produce a sharp late kick from a compressed sprint; the absence of any true pace-setter means the winner will come from whoever finds daylight first in the dash.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: London Is Blue Dictates
scenarios.trigger: If London Is Blue, despite a hold-up profile, is ridden to break smartly and find a prominent pitch given the pace vacuum.
scenarios.body: With no front-runner present, Jack Callan could exploit the tempo gap and secure a forward berth, using the horse's two wins on good ground over 6f as evidence of its ability to travel strongly and hold on.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Adalida Threads Through
scenarios.trigger: If Adalida, redistributed from true hold-up to midfield, manages to find a gap late and benefit from a well-timed Ethan Tindall ride.
scenarios.body: Adalida's most recent win came over this exact trip on good ground and the horse has shown sharp form when conditions suit, but the style-fit discount (0.92) is real — getting a clean run from a compressed sprint finish is not guaranteed.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Victor Cee Causes Upset
scenarios.trigger: If Victor Cee, a lower-rated outsider redistributed from hold-up to midfield, finds an uncontested line in a muddled sprint.
scenarios.body: Victor Cee's headgear flag and modest OR of 64 flag concern, and the style-fit discount (0.90) reflects genuine risk of being caught flat-footed in a sprint; however, in a field this small and slow-paced, even outsiders can find daylight.

watchPoints.text: With no natural front-runner, watch which jockey is first to commit for a forward position at the break — in a 4-runner 5f sprint, track position can be decisive and London Is Blue's Jack Callan may exploit the pace vacuum.

Adalida and Victor Cee are both true hold-up horses mapped to midfield — if the sprint bunches and gaps close, both face a significant risk of being blocked or finding no daylight in the final furlong.

Ambishio's headgear (hp) flags a horse that can be reluctant or inconsistent in its engagement; monitor whether Conor Whiteley (5lb claim) can get it racing forward enough in a slow-paced sprint to fire its kick at the right moment.

London Is Blue returns from a 79-day break — watch its paddock condition and whether it moves fluently to post; a lightly-raced 3yo returning off that layoff into a sharp 5f sprint on good ground could be ring-rusty at a crucial moment.

The going is listed as unknown throughout the card — any significant change from good could disproportionately affect Ambishio and London Is Blue, who both have their best form specifically on good ground at this trip.

races.name: Aeropak Restricted Maiden Stakes (For Horses In Bands B, C And D) (GBB Race)
4-head Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Gorgeous Mr George
runners_data.note: Won twice over 8f on Good ground recently, giving strong confidence in the surface and fitness; drops to 7f which may suit his stamina profile even better, and with no rivals likely to push him for the lead he holds the prime tactical position — Taryn Langley's 5lb claim helps offset the weight, though the Dylan Cunha yard is in a quiet spell at 0 from 19 over 14 days.
runners_data.comment: Won his last two starts after three eighths before that, a big turnaround rated 82 by us, third of six here, with today's distance covered from stall one. Quick to race again after 19 days, though that below-par spell before his revival is the concern.

runners_data.name: Sea Suite
runners_data.note: Cieren Fallon is a major positive booking and the form string includes a 7f Yarmouth win, giving genuine course-and-distance evidence; held up in rear by style with visor headgear suggesting a need for cover, and although similar-going figures are modest (1W from 14) the trip and jockey combination make this one to respect late.
runners_data.comment: Two wins in his last six starts underline solid ability, and our rating of 83 - the second-highest in this field - already comes with today's distance covered. A below-par seventh last time out and a 27-day gap since are the concerns.

runners_data.name: Tryst
runners_data.note: George Boughey's 3-year-old has been running over 10f and 8f in recent starts, so this drop to 7f is a significant shortening of trip that may or may not suit; the hold-up style backed by a tongue strap needs pace to aim at and the limited similar-going record (0W from 7) tempers enthusiasm, though Jack Callan's 3lb claim is a useful weight offset.
runners_data.comment: A win among her last five starts backs a rating of 90 from us, clear of this field, and she already has today's distance covered. A below-par sixth last time out, 33 days ago, is her only knock.

runners_data.name: Izzy Fast
runners_data.note: Solid recent form includes a 7f Yarmouth win on Good ground, making the track-and-trip profile compelling; by nature a hold-up horse who is shown in midfield on this map only because the field is congested with closers — Hector Crouch will need to find a clean run in a race where the pace may not be strong enough to set up a late charge.
runners_data.comment: Bottom of our ratings in this field of six leaves plenty to find on official figures, though a runner-up finish last time out and a quick return after just seven days are in her favour, with today's distance already covered.

runners_data.name: Up The Agenda
runners_data.note: Oisin Murphy's presence on a 3-year-old rated 75 is a significant upgrade in riding quality and this horse has won twice on Soft-to-Standard, handling fast ground adequately; a prominent racer by style who should get a clean position just off Gorgeous Mr George, with a visor fitted — the 6f wins suggest the 7f trip may stretch stamina slightly.
runners_data.comment: Two wins among his last five starts show he retains ability, and he already has today's distance covered, but his last two efforts - eighth and seventh - were well below that level after a 27-day break.

runners_data.name: Dion Baker
runners_data.note: Remarkable recent form with five wins from his last six starts all over 7f on Good ground at this very track, giving outstanding course-and-trip credentials; by inclination a prominent-racing type but the map places him in midfield due to pace congestion — that positional compromise is a genuine concern even with this level of course form, and the tongue strap signals he has needed managing.
runners_data.comment: Five wins from his last six starts is an eye-catching sequence, with a swift return after eight days and today's distance already covered, but he's only fifth of six on our rating here, leaving more to find against this field.

races.paceDynamic: Gorgeous Mr George is the one confirmed front-runner here and, crucially, faces no genuine challenger for the lead — Up The Agenda and Dion Baker carry prominent tendencies but both are likely to settle just off the pace rather than contest the front slot. That gives Gorgeous Mr George a chance to dictate an honest but uncontested gallop over seven furlongs at Yarmouth, a track where a controlled lead is a powerful weapon. The field holds more prominent and hold-up types than the map can accommodate naturally: Dion Baker and Izzy Fast are genuine pace-seeking horses pushed back by congestion, meaning they will not race where they are most effective. The race shape strongly favours a prominent-to-lead profile that can exploit a pressured but manageable pace — a horse sitting just behind Gorgeous Mr George in a smooth stalking position is ideally placed to pounce when the fractions begin to tell.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Gorgeous Mr George Controls
scenarios.trigger: If Gorgeous Mr George bowls along uncontested and sets a fair but sustainable pace, allowing a stalker to sit close and produce a clean run.
scenarios.body: Gorgeous Mr George dictates from the front with no genuine rivals willing to go with him, meaning fractions are controlled and the horse can dictate the tempo throughout the seven furlongs; horses sitting prominently just off the pace are perfectly positioned to challenge inside the final furlong when the leader's energy is spent.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Stalker Swamps Leader Late
scenarios.trigger: If Gorgeous Mr George does enough to use the lead but fades inside the final furlong as a prominent rival delivers a well-timed challenge.
scenarios.body: Gorgeous Mr George's recent fitness and course profile suggest he may be vulnerable late if the gallop is slightly stronger than ideal, leaving space for a horse sitting just off the pace to wear him down; Up The Agenda or Sea Suite, who can travel prominently, are best placed to capitalise in this shape.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Finishes Through
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely strong enough to create a true gap for closers to exploit in the final two furlongs.
scenarios.body: This shape requires the gallop to be hotter than a lone front-runner scenario typically produces at Yarmouth, making it an unlikely but non-zero outcome; Sea Suite and Tryst carry the most credible hold-up profiles in the field, but both face the challenge of Yarmouth's flat, undemanding straight not always generating the sustained pace needed.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse, Chaos
scenarios.trigger: If multiple horses contest the early lead aggressively, causing a scramble that fractures the field and leaves no one with a clean run.
scenarios.body: Dion Baker and Izzy Fast, both true pace-seeking types operating out of their natural position, could complicate matters if either decides to push forward against expectation, creating uncharacteristic early pressure; in this messy shape, a horse with tactical speed and a capable jockey — Cieren Fallon aboard Sea Suite — could pick through a disrupted field.

watchPoints.text: Gorgeous Mr George is likely to get an uncontested lead — watch whether Taryn Langley elects to use that advantage aggressively or tries to conserve, as the decision will define the pace shape of the entire race.

Dion Baker has outstanding course form but is a natural prominent racer likely to be denied his ideal spot — watch the early furlong to see if Darragh Keenan pushes forward against the map, which would significantly increase early pressure.

Izzy Fast is a genuine hold-up type mapped to midfield due to congestion — Hector Crouch will need a clean passage through horses, and any traffic trouble in the straight could cost this runner dearly.

Sea Suite carries visor headgear and Cieren Fallon is a strong booking — watch how early Fallon commits for his run, as Yarmouth's flat straight can catch out horses who leave their challenge too late.

Tryst's trip drop from 10f-8f to 7f is the most significant distance change in the field — watch the betting market for any late move that would suggest connections believe the shorter trip unlocks something.

races.name: Doublebase Classified Stakes

runners_data.name: Duke Orsino
runners_data.note: A genuine hold-up horse with poor recent form (0-4-4-5 in last five) and no wins or places on good going in six attempts at similar conditions; Jonny Peate and J.R. Jenkins have a blank 14-day record and the horse's natural rear-of-field style will be cramped in this field, reducing its chance of getting the run it needs.
runners_data.comment: Yet to win in five starts, fifth last time out after finishing fourth in each of his previous two, with today's distance covered. Rated only 44 by us, fifth of seven here, and a below-par ninth further back in that run is the low point.

runners_data.name: Highland Harvey
runners_data.note: Has shown consistent placed form at 12f on good and standard going (two seconds, two thirds in five runs), which is the most encouraging profile in the field for this trip, but the ⚠ fade flag is a serious concern in what may become a sprint finish; Ray Dawson rides for a trainer with a modest 1/4 recent strike rate.
runners_data.comment: Runner-up last time out with two further places in this five-start sequence, Highland Harvey is the most consistent sort and tops our figures at 53, with today's distance already covered. Yet to win in that time, and a below-par ninth further back is the blemish.

runners_data.name: Spaceage Love Song
runners_data.note: Won at 12f on standard ground and placed on good, giving her the most relevant recent form, and Oisin Murphy is the standout jockey booking in this field — the visor (v headgear) adds a wild-card element; mapped to mid-division despite hold-up instincts, but Murphy's tactical intelligence is the key asset if this race lacks pace.
runners_data.comment: Runner-up last time out just seven days ago, Spaceage Love Song won earlier in this six-start sequence and already has today's distance covered. Rated 49 by us, third of seven here, with a couple of moderate efforts in between the concern.

runners_data.name: Suitcase Smith
runners_data.note: David Egan is a strong jockey appointment in a modest classified stakes field, and Suitcase Smith's six good-going runs at 12f offer solid trip experience; the horse has not won or placed on good going from those attempts, but this grade may present the best opportunity yet.
runners_data.comment: Rated the second-highest in this field by us, well above what a run of finishes without a placing suggests, Suitcase Smith already has today's distance covered. He was sixth last time out and is up against a 24-day break, the main concerns.

runners_data.name: Ten Ten Twenty
runners_data.note: The veteran (age 8) carries the best going-adjusted form — one win and three places from six runs on similar ground — and has distance experience out to 16f, meaning a truly-run race would suit; the 74-day absence and tongue-strap (tp) are worth monitoring, but the trip record is the most solid in the race.
runners_data.comment: Third last time out, his best effort in a run of modest finishes, Ten Ten Twenty already has today's distance covered. A 74-day absence since and a rating of 46 from us, fourth of seven, are the concerns.

runners_data.name: Cormorant Rock
runners_data.note: The youngest in the field (3yo) with limited experience (four runs) and all form at shorter trips of 8f-10f, making this step up to 1m3½f a significant unknown; Jim Boyle has a modest recent record and the horse's redistribution into mid-division means it must produce its effort from an unfamiliar race position as well as an unfamiliar trip.
runners_data.comment: Bottom of our ratings, with a run of finishes short on places, Cormorant Rock has plenty to prove. A fourth was his best effort in that time, though he returns quickly after six days, and his speed figure of 54 is a shade more encouraging.

runners_data.name: Fletcher
runners_data.note: Another Jim Boyle-trained 3yo stepping into a field of older and more experienced horses, with seven recent runs all at 10f-12f on good to soft ground showing no wins or places; Pat Cosgrave rides and the horse's natural hold-up profile is compressed by the lack of any front-runners in this field, adding further positional uncertainty to an already modest form profile.
runners_data.comment: Rated only sixth of seven in this field, Fletcher's recent finishes - seventh last time out, sixth and seventh before that - leave little to catch the eye, though today's distance is already covered. A fourth further back, after 14 days off, is the one positive.

races.paceDynamic: With every single runner in this seven-horse field carrying a hold-up profile, there is no confirmed front-runner and no horse with a genuine desire to lead — meaning the early gallop will almost certainly be pedestrian, with runners jostling for position in a slowly-run, bunched affair over 1m3½f at Yarmouth. The race is likely to crawl into the home straight before erupting into a sprint-style finish from the two-furlong pole, favouring whoever can produce the sharpest turn of foot from a compressed pack. Horses showing any evidence of a mid-race kick or a strong cruising speed — rather than pure staying stamina — will be best placed to capitalise on this shape. The field holds more genuine hold-up types than can all sit last, so horses like Spaceage Love Song, Highland Harvey, Fletcher, Duke Orsino, and Cormorant Rock will be shuffled into mid-division against their instincts, with Ten Ten Twenty and Suitcase Smith — both natural stalkers — perhaps best positioned to exploit a truly muddling gallop; the tactical verdict firmly favours horses with a proven turn of foot who handle a sprint finish rather than resolute stayers who need a true pace.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Sprint Finish From Pack
scenarios.trigger: If the pace crawls and the race ignites only in the final two furlongs, producing a mass cavalry charge.
scenarios.body: The tightly bunched field sweeps around the home turn together and the outcome is decided by raw acceleration over a short distance, rendering stamina largely irrelevant. Ten Ten Twenty, who has form at this trip and has shown the ability to quicken from a stalking position, and Spaceage Love Song, with Oisin Murphy able to find the best position in a compressed field, are ideally suited.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Strongest Stayer Grinds Out
scenarios.trigger: If an unexpectedly strong gallop develops — perhaps two horses disputing — and the race becomes a genuine test of stamina over the full 1m3½f.
scenarios.body: A true-run race filters out the sprinters and rewards the horse with the best combination of stamina and racing class for this trip and grade, producing a decisive winning margin from those who travel well. Ten Ten Twenty's proven form over 12f-16f and Highland Harvey's consistent placed record at 12f in good ground make them the most credible finishers if the race is run to suit stayers.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Murphy Dictates On Spaceage
scenarios.trigger: If Oisin Murphy uses Spaceage Love Song's class edge and his own tactical intelligence to push forward and control a race with no natural leader.
scenarios.body: Murphy seizes the initiative from the front or just off it, setting a controlled pace that suits his mount and produces a winning break before the field can respond — the absence of any genuine front-runner makes this position easy to secure. Spaceage Love Song's win on good ground at 12f and OR of 49 represent a ceiling in this field, and if Murphy sends her forward she may never be caught.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Closers Outpaced In Bunched Finish
scenarios.trigger: If the sprint finish unfolds but the redistribution of true hold-up types into mid-division leaves several horses unable to produce their best effort from an unnatural position.
scenarios.body: Horses forced into unfamiliar roles — Duke Orsino, Fletcher, and Cormorant Rock — fail to find their rhythm or produce their finishing effort from the wrong part of the field, and the race falls to whichever runner best handles the chaotic, compressed nature of the finish. Suitcase Smith with David Egan, perhaps the most versatile tactically, and Cormorant Rock as the youngest and potentially most physically progressive, could emerge if others over-race.

watchPoints.text: Watch Oisin Murphy on Spaceage Love Song — with no natural front-runner in the field, Murphy may take the initiative and push forward from the outset, entirely changing the race shape from a sprint finish to a controlled small-field test.

Watch the early gallop closely — if no horse shows any desire to lead in the first two furlongs, the pace could be dangerously slow, compressing the entire field and making draw position and jockey reactions in the straight decisive.

Highland Harvey is flagged as a horse that fades in the finish, which is a significant concern if this race becomes the sprint-style finish that the pace map suggests; Ray Dawson will need to time the challenge perfectly to prevent the fade arriving before the line.

Ten Ten Twenty has been off for 74 days and wears a tongue-strap — monitor in the pre-parade ring for any signs of freshness or rustiness, as the layoff could affect how Cieren Fallon is able to deploy the horse in what may be a chaotic, fast-finishing race.

Both Jim Boyle runners (Cormorant Rock and Fletcher) are 3yos stepping up significantly in trip against older horses — watch whether either travels comfortably in the early stages, as struggling to settle or fading early would confirm the trip is beyond them at this stage of their development.

races.name: Bazuka Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Dark Side Thunder
runners_data.note: Genuine hold-up horse who has placed four times in five runs at 6f on good ground, making this trip and surface squarely in his wheelhouse; the visor is in place and at 25 days since his last run he arrives fresh, but the 0-from-15 strike rate on similar going is a sobering caution.
runners_data.comment: Our top-rated runner, with a second and a third among his last six starts and today's trip already covered. Fresh after 25 days off, he's yet to win in that sequence but the form is solid enough to be feared.

runners_data.name: Startled Lady
runners_data.note: A filly with three placed efforts on good ground and strong course-and-distance credentials, and Neil Callan's booking gives her a tactical edge in a field where position will be hard to find; her trainer William Knight is in good recent form at 3/19 over 14 days, and this looks her most suitable surface.
runners_data.comment: A second and two thirds feature among her last five starts without landing that elusive win. Fresh after a 25-day break and already proven over today's trip, she's the leading danger on our figures but needs more late to turn those places around.

runners_data.name: Viking Glory
runners_data.note: Has failed to win in seven attempts on good ground and shaped poorly on his last two starts at 5f and 6f; his natural running style is as a hold-up horse but the saturated rear of this field means he is squeezed toward midfield against his wishes, which compounds an already modest recent profile.
runners_data.comment: Two unplaced efforts sandwiched around a 7th mark his last three starts, well below the third and fifth found further back. Thirty days since his last run and already proven over today's trip, he's the classic each-way danger if he can rediscover that earlier form.

runners_data.name: Lieutenant Sir
runners_data.note: Won most recently on good ground over this exact trip at 6f and Oisin Murphy is a significant jockey booking that demands respect; though he is a genuine come-from-behind horse by nature, Murphy may well elect to exploit the vacant front end, and his 6-day turnaround suggests he is race-fit and ready.
runners_data.comment: Unplaced last time out, though he won the start before that and has run over today's distance. Back after just six days, but the yard is 0 from 21 in the last fortnight and he rates fifth of six on our figures.

runners_data.name: Komodo Rose
runners_data.note: Has run exclusively at 7f recently and a drop to 6f on an unconfirmed going strip at Yarmouth is a genuine concern, with her last win also coming at the longer trip on standard; her true style is as a hold-up horse, but she is already shuffled toward a crowded midfield berth, and the headgear switch (p) adds a layer of uncertainty.
runners_data.comment: Rated the outsider of the six, having failed to fire last time and managed only a 6th before that. A second still features among her last four starts, but she's yet to win and a 35-day gap since her latest run is a further concern.

runners_data.name: Superstorm
runners_data.note: Most recent start was 16 days ago, making her the freshest runner in the field, and trainer Charlie Fellowes has struck at 3/12 over the past fortnight; a hold-up horse by inclination who has been competing at 7f, the drop back to 6f may be sharp, but she has placed at this distance before and the visor has been applied to sharpen her response.
runners_data.comment: A second and third feature among his last five starts, underlining the untapped potential our figures see in him. Freshened by a 16-day break and already proven over today's trip, though back-to-back 6ths in his most recent two runs are the note of caution.

races.paceDynamic: With all six runners carrying a hold-up profile and no confirmed front-runner in the field, this 6f Yarmouth handicap is set to drift into a slow-burn, sprint-finish affair where the pace is likely to be tentative early before a furlong-and-a-half scramble to the line. The absence of any natural leader means the early gallop will be modest at best, with runners eyeing each other cautiously before the race ignites in the final two furlongs — a shape that theoretically suits horses who can accelerate late but critically requires genuine closing ability, not just a hold-up position on paper. Dark Side Thunder and Startled Lady are the only two runners whose hold-up mapping reflects their true running style, giving them a meaningful positional advantage in this shape. The field is almost entirely composed of hold-up types, with Viking Glory, Lieutenant Sir, Komodo Rose, and Superstorm all genuine come-from-behind horses who cannot all find their natural position and will be forced to negotiate each other in a compressed sprint finish — in such a race, the horses with the cleanest late kick and most consistent form on good ground hold the edge, and the profile that benefits most is the true closer with strong course-and-distance form and a proven turn of foot on good turf.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Sprint Finish Suits Closers
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely slow and the race becomes a flat-out dash from the two-furlong pole, rewarding the sharpest late accelerator.
scenarios.body: With no pace-setter to set the tempo, the field compresses and the race becomes a cavalry charge where reaction speed and finishing punch decide the outcome; runners who have placed consistently on good ground at 6f are best placed.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Traffic Chaos Aids Brave Racer
scenarios.trigger: If the congested hold-up pack causes interference and one runner threads a clear run from off the pace to strike late.
scenarios.body: The redistribution of so many genuine hold-up types into the same slice of the race creates a real danger of blocked runs and checked momentum; the runner who secures daylight earliest in the straight gains a decisive advantage.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: One Runner Steals Breakaway
scenarios.trigger: If one jockey decides to set a tempo from the front and controls the fractions unchallenged with no natural rivals for the lead.
scenarios.body: With no horse bred or trained to dominate from the front, an opportunistic prominent move from a redistributed runner could create a wire-to-wire scenario against a field of reluctant front-runners; Lieutenant Sir's one win came front-to-front and Oisin Murphy has the tactical intelligence to exploit a vacant lead.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Poor Surface Scramble
scenarios.trigger: If the unknown going proves slower or more testing than expected, turning the finish into an attritional grind that exposes fitness differences.
scenarios.body: The going report is entirely unconfirmed at Yarmouth, and if the ground is softer than anticipated, runners with a genuine preference for testing conditions and recent sharpness gain an edge; Superstorm has placed on soft and standard and is only 16 days since its last run.

watchPoints.text: With no front-runner in this field, watch for an extremely slow early gallop that compresses the race into a two-furlong sprint — any runner drawn widest may find themselves stuck out and exposed.

Lieutenant Sir with Oisin Murphy bears close watching at the start: if Murphy opts to stride forward and seize the uncontested lead, the entire race shape flips and the hold-up field will be caught flat-footed.

Viking Glory, Komodo Rose, and Superstorm are all genuine hold-up horses forced into a congested midfield section — watch for traffic trouble at the two-furlong pole if the field fans wide simultaneously.

Dark Side Thunder is a 0-from-15 horse on similar going despite multiple placed efforts; the form looks enticing but the win conversion rate in this exact scenario should temper expectations materially.

The going at Yarmouth is completely unconfirmed across all six declarations — if overnight rain has affected the surface, runners with soft-ground form such as Superstorm could be significantly more relevant than their current market position implies.
